Care Plan for Patient P1001 — Total Knee Replacement

Patient: Alex Morgan (fictional — all data synthetic)
Patient ID: P1001
Date of Birth: 1958-06-14 (fictional)
Procedure: Total Knee Replacement (Right Knee)
Surgery Date: 2024-01-18
Surgeon: Dr. Patricia Holloway (fictional)
Primary Care Physician: Dr. Samuel Reeves (fictional)
Case Manager: Jennifer Tran, RN (fictional)

Diagnosis: Advanced osteoarthritis of the right knee with complete loss of joint space, causing significant functional impairment and failure to respond to conservative management.

Procedure Summary: The patient underwent elective total right knee replacement using a cemented tricompartmental implant under spinal anesthesia. The procedure was uncomplicated. Estimated blood loss was within normal limits. The patient was transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit in stable condition.

Goals of Care:
1. Achieve full wound healing without infection within 4 weeks.
2. Attain at least 120 degrees of knee flexion by 8 weeks post-surgery.
3. Return to independent ambulation without an assistive device by 10–12 weeks.
4. Maintain anticoagulation therapy as prescribed to prevent deep vein thrombosis.
5. Resume all baseline activities of daily living within 3 months.

Medication Plan:
The patient is prescribed the following medications at discharge. See the patient-p1001-medications document for full details.
- Warfarin 5 mg daily (anticoagulation — dose to be adjusted based on INR monitoring)
- Oxycodone/Acetaminophen 5/325 mg every 4–6 hours as needed for pain (maximum 6 tablets/day)
- Acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours scheduled for baseline pain control
- Pantoprazole 40 mg daily for gastrointestinal protection
- Docusate Sodium 100 mg twice daily for constipation prevention

Important: The patient must avoid ibuprofen, naproxen, and all NSAIDs while on warfarin. Combining warfarin with NSAIDs significantly increases the risk of serious bleeding events.

Anticoagulation Monitoring Schedule:
- INR check on 2024-01-25 (7 days post-surgery)
- INR check on 2024-02-01 (14 days post-surgery)
- INR check on 2024-02-15 (4 weeks post-surgery)
- Target INR range: 2.0–3.0

Follow-Up Appointment Schedule:
- 2024-02-01: Post-operative wound check with Dr. Holloway; staple removal; review INR; physical therapy progress review
- 2024-03-15: Six-week functional assessment; range of motion evaluation; imaging review; transition to outpatient physical therapy if not already initiated
- 2024-04-18: Three-month milestone visit; functional outcome scoring; activity clearance assessment
- 2024-07-18: Six-month implant stability review with X-rays
- 2025-01-18: One-year annual review

Physical Therapy Plan:
Patient is enrolled in home physical therapy beginning 2024-01-20 (2 days post-discharge). Home PT visits are scheduled 3 times per week for 4 weeks. Transition to outpatient PT anticipated at the 2024-02-01 visit. Physical therapy goals: achieve 90 degrees of flexion by 2024-02-01, 110 degrees by 2024-03-01, and 120 degrees by 2024-03-15.

Care Tasks and Timeline:
- 2024-01-20 to 2024-02-01: Perform prescribed home exercises twice daily; keep wound clean and dry; take all medications as scheduled; perform daily ankle pumps to prevent DVT; apply ice 3–4 times per day for swelling.
- 2024-02-01 to 2024-03-15: Transition to outpatient PT; wean from walker to cane as tolerated; increase walking distance daily; continue warfarin and INR monitoring.
- 2024-03-15 to 2024-04-18: Home exercise program without formal PT; resume light daily activities; no high-impact activities.
- 2024-04-18 onwards: Clearance for driving, return to work (sedentary), and gradual return to recreational activities as tolerated.

Escalation Conditions:
The following conditions require immediate action. Verbatim escalation language from care plan:

"Contact your surgeon immediately if you experience fever above 101°F, increased redness around the incision, or sudden severe pain."

"Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately if you experience chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, or calf pain with swelling, as these may indicate a pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis."

"Contact your anticoagulation clinic or surgeon immediately if you experience unusual bleeding, including blood in urine, black or tarry stools, or bleeding that does not stop within 10 minutes."

Home Support Arrangements:
The patient will reside with a family member (fictional: adult child) during the initial recovery period. Home health aide visits are arranged for days 1–14 post-discharge for activities of daily living support. Patient education has been completed and acknowledged in writing.
